findings.summary: The history that justifies pulling `presign` into scope is backwards -- presign arrived 15 hours AFTER the M5.29 row was written, not before it -- and the false sentence is restated in three places
findings.detail: The diff argues its one piece of unnamed scope three times: FaultInjectingStore.java:172-174 ('The M5.29 row named two of the three; the third had already arrived, which is the argument for separating the jobs rather than adding a fourth exception'), FaultInjectingStoreTest.java:78-80 ('the third had already arrived by the time it was written, which is the row's own argument...'), and the backlog M5.29 status cell at docs/internal/product/backlog.md:38 ('`presign` had already arrived by the time it was written'). MEASURED against this repository's own history: the M5.29 row first appears in b44817a (M5.26, 2026-09-10 09:34:48 +1000) -- `git show b44817a~1:docs/internal/product/backlog.md | grep -c '^| M5.29'` is 0 -- and it has not been edited since. `presign` first appears in FaultInjectingStore.java in d5b5f21 (M5.10, 2026-09-11 00:42:06 +1000); `git show 0e0db0f:.../FaultInjectingStore.java | grep -c presign` is 0. So presign arrived roughly fifteen hours AFTER the row, and under the only reading that makes the sentence an argument ('it' = the row, per the following clause 'the row's own argument') all three statements are false. Failure scenario: a later hand auditing why presign was in a task whose row names only `capabilities` and `close` checks the history, finds the stated justification contradicted by two commits, and has no way to tell that from the surrounding measured claims -- which I re-ran and found all true (1,608 / 0 / 38 / 12 unmutated on both trees, 85,458 readers identical, 1,626 green on HEAD under the `store.stat(leases.key())` swap, 0 and red on this tree). This milestone has already spent a round on exactly this (review/overrides.md M5.26 round four: 'round three's corrections were themselves wrong ... it also introduced a fresh falsehood'), and M5.27 exists as a row solely because quotes went stale. ⚠️ THE TRUE HISTORY IS THE STRONGER ARGUMENT and the fix is one sentence in each of the three places: the row predicted 'both are staleness the next verb makes real', and the next verb -- presign, M5.10, the next day -- made it real before anyone touched the row. That is a measured instance of the predicted failure rather than an oversight in the row.
findings.failure_scenario: A later hand audits why `presign` is in a task whose row names only `capabilities` and `close`, reads 'the third had already arrived by the time it was written', checks the history, and finds it contradicted: the row is b44817a (2026-09-10 09:34:48) and presign is d5b5f21 (2026-09-11 00:42:06). The scope decision is right, but its stated ground is false in three places including the permanent backlog record, so the reader cannot tell it apart from the surrounding claims -- which I re-measured and found all true.

findings.summary: The new `byVerb` field is declared between `refuseIfPartitioned`'s javadoc and the method, so that javadoc now documents a counting map -- the same defect M5.26's round three fixed in this file
findings.detail: Lines 208-216 are the javadoc for `refuseIfPartitioned` ('Refuses the call if the acting pod is partitioned. ⚠️ EVERY VERB, not only the writes. A partition is a network fact ... the thing that makes a zombie a zombie'). The diff inserts `private final Map<String, Integer> byVerb = new java.util.LinkedHashMap<>();` at line 217, between that block and the method at line 219. Javadoc and every IDE now bind that text to `byVerb`, and `refuseIfPartitioned` -- whose 'EVERY VERB' clause is the reason a partitioned leader cannot read its own fencing -- is left undocumented. Worse in this diff than in general: on a counting map, 'EVERY VERB, not only the writes' reads as a claim about what is COUNTED, which is the very confusion between counting and refusing that M5.29 exists to end. Failure scenario: the next reader asking why `capabilities` is counted but not refused greps for the partition rationale and finds it attached to the ledger. Note review/overrides.md:71 records 'a field declaration that landed between a javadoc and the method it documents' as a round-three finding on M5.26 in this same file; this reintroduces it. Fix is to move the declaration up to the other fields (or below the method).
findings.failure_scenario: The next reader asking why `capabilities` is counted but not refused greps for the partition rationale, and javadoc/IDE hand them 'EVERY VERB, not only the writes' attached to the `byVerb` counting map rather than to `refuseIfPartitioned`, which is left undocumented -- so the sentence reads as a claim about what is COUNTED, the exact confusion between counting and refusing this task exists to end.

findings.summary: `record(verb)` at the top of every verb is a remember-to rule with nothing enforcing it, so the staleness M5.29 closes returns the next time a verb is added
findings.detail: All twelve overrides carry a `record(...)` today -- verified against BinStore's eleven methods plus `close` -- so the claim 'every verb' holds on this tree. But nothing fails if the thirteenth omits it: `calls(String)` is `byVerb.getOrDefault(verb, 0)`, so an unrecorded verb reads as 0, and the new tests only exercise stat/putIfMatch/capabilities/close. Failure scenario: the next `default` method added to the BinStore SPI is overridden here (as presign was at M5.10) without a `record` call; if any release path later comes to rest on it, `GracefulReleaseMeter.released()` credits nothing and CommitProtocolSweepTest's `gracefulReleases >= SEEDS` floor reds at a fraction of 1,608 with no defect present -- the same false-red the M5.29 row was opened to remove, one verb later. This is gate-design rung 7 (an instruction an author must remember) where rung 3 is available cheaply: a reflective T0 case that invokes every public BinStore method on the decorator and asserts `calls()` rose, which would have caught presign's escape without a review round. AGENTS.md non-negotiable 9 asks for one sentence saying why rungs 1-5 cannot carry it; the diff does not say. Recording as a row rather than widening this commit is a fine answer.
findings.failure_scenario: The next verb added to FaultInjectingStore (as `presign` was added at M5.10, after this row was written) omits its `record(...)` line. Nothing in the tree fails: `calls(String)` returns 0 for an unrecorded verb and the new cases cover only stat/putIfMatch/capabilities/close. If a release path later comes to rest on that verb, `released()` credits nothing and CommitProtocolSweepTest's `gracefulReleases >= SEEDS` floor reds far below 1,608 with no defect present -- the false-red M5.29 was opened to remove, one verb later.
